title: Knowledge check: Professional R Project Workflow

questions.prompt: For “Professional R Project Workflow”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.
Change several unrelated parts at once so the cause of any result is unclear.
questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: Professional R Project Workflow is one step in Security, Deployment, and Professional Practice; production readiness includes more than a successful local script: dependencies, permissions, observability, recovery and privacy matter. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Professional R Project Workflow” in the source curriculum?
options: Change unrelated settings before checking the input
Assume one example proves every edge case
Skip validation when the output looks plausible
questions.explanation: The source PDF lists “Clarifying the Analytical Objective” as part of lesson 247. The lesson retains the original topic wording.

questions.prompt: When applying “Professional R Project Workflow” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
Assume missing and malformed inputs never occur.
Use the same method regardless of data type or the research question.
Remove inconvenient observations without recording the decision.
questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Avoid secrets in code, document provenance, test release artifacts, and establish safe rollback and support procedures. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.

answer_key_visibility: Server-side only; API should return prompts/options without answer keys or explanations.
